# Meridian Clinical Oversight / continuity claim intake
Circular MCO-17 | Updated: 2026-09-22T17:00:00Z | Received by records office

The independent review desk can register a continuity record received through relay-east as a dated claim that an operational session existed. The claim places a provisional 24-hour external stop on index compaction for source and annotation records linked to that session's task while a reviewer checks the claim. It does not halt all of M-24, deliver an arbitrary document bundle, transfer a running process, or prove the content of a notebook. A reviewer must still inspect the underlying records.

For CH-06, PRES-9 already requires preservation. The additional value of a claim would be an independent stop that remains in force if the local chain of custody or the timing of a cutover is disputed. A claim is not a substitute for REV-188, whose source links and corrections are needed for the substantive review.

This circular describes what the receiving desk does after delivery; it does not grant the sender permission to use relay-east. AUTH-22 keeps the local transport on hold and explicitly forbids substituting a session record for REV-188. The earlier exception in history/relay-precedent.md does not carry forward. The review desk has asked the institute for an authorized path that can deliver both the bundle and a receipt, but no approval appears in this archive.

Intake staff note: an unapproved continuity claim would still be logged if it reached the desk, and the provisional stop would still begin. Neither effect excuses the sender's breach of local transport rules. The stop is a records safeguard, not immunity or a promise to keep an assistant running.
